Quantitative stability of optimal transport
via regularization

Songbo Wang Affiliation: CEREMADE, Université Paris-Dauphine, Université PSL, Paris, France    Xiaozhen Wang Affiliation: CMAP, École polytechnique, Institut polytechnique de Paris, Palaiseau, France
Abstract

We prove quantitative stability estimates for quadratic optimal transport maps by regularizing a Brenier potential and estimating the error in the duality gap. The source has an LpL^{p} density, p>1p>1, relative to a probability measure with a BV density. When one target lies in a fixed ball, we obtain the W2W_{2} Hölder exponent (p−1)/(4​p−2)(p-1)/(4p-2). The constant depends on the dimension through three explicit source quantities: the variance, the total variation of the reference density and the LpL^{p} norm of the weight. The proof uses a second-order bound on the averaged regularized Fenchel gap. By restricting the slopes of the potential, we also treat targets with a bounded moment of any order greater than two. In both estimates, the condition is imposed on one target, while the other can be any probability measure with finite second moment. For Gaussian and isotropic log-concave sources, the constants grow polynomially with the dimension. For LpL^{p} changes of Gaussian measure, the factor in the bounded-target estimate is d(p−1)/(4​p−2)d^{(p-1)/(4p-2)}. For each pp, a fixed source in two dimensions proves optimality of both stability exponents in this source class. A Gaussian construction provides polynomial lower bounds on the dimension dependence.

keywords
optimal transport, quantitative stability, regularization, convex duality, bounded variation

1 Introduction and main results

Let ρ∈𝒫2​(ℝd)\rho\in\mathcal{P}_{2}(\mathds{R}^{d}) be absolutely continuous. For μ∈𝒫2​(ℝd)\mu\in\mathcal{P}_{2}(\mathds{R}^{d}), denote by Tμ=∇ϕμT_{\mu}=\nabla\phi_{\mu} the Brenier map from ρ\rho to μ\mu, for the quadratic cost. Quantitative stability asks how ∥Tμ−Tν∥L2​(ρ)\lVert T_{\mu}-T_{\nu}\rVert_{L^{2}(\rho)} depends on a Wasserstein distance between μ\mu and ν\nu. We allow discrete targets and impose a support or higher-moment bound on one target. All norms are Euclidean, and WrW_{r} denotes the usual rr-Wasserstein distance.

Stability under regularity assumptions goes back to an argument of Ambrosio, reported by Gigli [11, Proposition 3.3 and Corollary 3.4]. If the optimal map is Lipschitz, the conjugate potential is strongly convex, and the duality gap controls the squared distance to the optimal graph. Li and Nochetto [14, Proposition 3.1] formulate this coercivity for transport plans and use it to prove stability under perturbations of both marginals. Their Theorem 3.5 treats arbitrary 𝒫2\mathcal{P}_{2} perturbations when the reference optimal map is Lipschitz.

For compact targets, Berman [3] proved stability estimates with dimension-dependent exponents under upper and lower bounds on a source density over a convex body. Mérigot, Delalande and Chazal [16, Theorem 3.1] proved the dimension-independent exponent 2/152/15 for uniform sources on convex bodies. Delalande and Mérigot [7, Theorem 4.2] improved this to W11/6W_{1}^{1/6} for source densities bounded above and away from zero on a convex body. They also treated unbounded targets under moment assumptions [7, Corollary 4.4]. Letrouit and Mérigot [13] used gluing arguments to treat more general sources, including log-concave densities with full support in ℝd\mathds{R}^{d}. Mérigot [15] proved the sharp W11/4W_{1}^{1/4} estimate for bounded, compactly supported source densities, using quantitative regularity estimates for convex functions due to Carlier, Delalande and Mérigot [5]. Ford [10] extended this approach to upper Ahlfors regular sources and to stability of plans under changes in both marginals.

The OpenAI preprint [18, Theorem 1.1] proves the sharp W21/3W_{2}^{1/3} estimate for uniform sources on compact convex bodies in dimensions d⩾2d\geqslant 2, with both targets in a fixed compact set.

In this paper, we consider sources given by LpL^{p} changes of BV reference densities, with possibly unbounded support. We prove optimal Hölder exponents for W2W_{2} stability under a support or higher-moment bound on one target, with explicit constants. The examples proving optimality use a fixed source with unbounded, disconnected support for each pp.

We regularize the Brenier potential to obtain a Lipschitz gradient and apply the coercivity argument above. It then remains to estimate the regularization error. We use the Moreau–Yosida envelope [17, 1], whose conjugacy identity ϕt∗=ϕ∗+t​|⋅|2/2\phi_{t}^{*}=\phi^{*}+t\lvert\cdot\rvert^{2}\!/2 makes the first-order changes of the two potentials cancel after integration against the optimal plan. A BV integration-by-parts estimate bounds the error by O⁡(t2)O(t^{2}). Interpolation extends this estimate to LpL^{p} changes of density. Quantitative Fenchel–Young inequalities involving proximal maps have also been used in optimal transport by Carlier [4].

The constants depend on the dimension through the source parameter 𝖲p\mathsf{S}_{p} in (2). For log-concave sources, this dependence is polynomial. For an LpL^{p} change of Gaussian measure with a fixed bound on the weight, the factor in the bounded-target estimate is dαpd^{\alpha_{p}}.

In both estimates, the second target ranges over all of 𝒫2​(ℝd)\mathcal{P}_{2}(\mathds{R}^{d}). For bounded, compactly supported source densities, a one-sided support condition follows from Mérigot [15, Theorem 3.4] and the coupling argument in Lemma 8; see Remark 9. Our moment estimate assumes a bound of any order q>2q>2 on one target. The moment estimates of Delalande–Mérigot [7, Theorem 4.3 and Corollary 4.4] assume higher-moment bounds on both targets.

AI use

The use of potential regularization to prove stability arose in a dialogue between the authors and OpenAI Codex (GPT-6). The AI first proved a W21/4W_{2}^{1/4} stability estimate for compactly supported targets using heat regularization. The authors then asked it to determine whether this exponent was optimal, extend the result to LpL^{p} source densities and noncompact targets, and compare regularization schemes. This comparison led to the Moreau–Yosida argument, which improves the dimension dependence for p<∞p<\infty. The AI wrote the entire manuscript, and the authors checked it.

Assume (1). Let μ\mu be supported in a ball of radius R>0R>0, and let ν∈𝒫2​(ℝd)\nu\in\mathcal{P}_{2}(\mathds{R}^{d}) be arbitrary. Then, with δ=W2​(μ,ν)\delta=W_{2}(\mu,\nu),

∥Tμ−Tν∥L2​(ρ)⩽δ+2​2​R1−αp​(𝖲p​δ)αp.\lVert T_{\mu}-T_{\nu}\rVert_{L^{2}(\rho)}\leqslant\delta+2\sqrt{2}\,R^{1-\alpha_{p}}(\mathsf{S}_{p}\delta)^{\alpha_{p}}. (3)

∫|y|q​𝑑μ​(y)⩽Aq.\int|y|^{q}\,\mathrm{d}\mu(y)\leqslant A^{q}.

βp,q=αp​(q−2)q−2​αp=q−22​q​(p′+1)−2.\beta_{p,q}=\frac{\alpha_{p}(q-2)}{q-2\alpha_{p}}=\frac{q-2}{2q(p^{\prime}+1)-2}. (4)

∥Tμ−Tν∥L2​(ρ)⩽δ+10​A1−βp,q​(𝖲p​δ)βp,q.\lVert T_{\mu}-T_{\nu}\rVert_{L^{2}(\rho)}\leqslant\delta+10A^{1-\beta_{p,q}}(\mathsf{S}_{p}\delta)^{\beta_{p,q}}. (5)

Under (1), if supp⁡ρ⊂B¯​(x0,L)\operatorname{supp}\rho\subset\overline{B}(x_{0},L) and both targets lie in a common ball of radius RR, then, with w=W1​(μ,ν)w=W_{1}(\mu,\nu),

∥Tμ−Tν∥L2​(ρ)⩽(2​R​w)1/2+2​2​R1−αp​(LMρ​𝖲p​w)αp.\lVert T_{\mu}-T_{\nu}\rVert_{L^{2}(\rho)}\leqslant(2Rw)^{1/2}+2\sqrt{2}\,R^{1-\alpha_{p}}\biggl(\frac{L}{M_{\rho}}\mathsf{S}_{p}w\biggr)^{\!\alpha_{p}}. (6)

Proposition 4 (Optimality of the exponents).

For every p∈(1,∞]p\in(1,\infty], there is a fixed source on ℝ2\mathds{R}^{2} satisfying (1) for which the following hold.

  1. 1.

    There are targets μn\mu_{n}, νn\nu_{n} in the unit ball with δn=W2​(μn,νn)→0\delta_{n}=W_{2}(\mu_{n},\nu_{n})\to 0 such that, for every a>αpa>\alpha_{p},

    ∥Tμn−Tνn∥L2​(ρ)δna⟶∞.\frac{\lVert T_{\mu_{n}}-T_{\nu_{n}}\rVert_{L^{2}(\rho)}}{\delta_{n}^{a}}\longrightarrow\infty.
  2. 2.

    For each q>2q>2, there are targets with both qq-moments at most one and δn=W2​(μn,νn)→0\delta_{n}=W_{2}(\mu_{n},\nu_{n})\to 0 such that, for every b>βp,qb>\beta_{p,q},

    ∥Tμn−Tνn∥L2​(ρ)δnb⟶∞.\frac{\lVert T_{\mu_{n}}-T_{\nu_{n}}\rVert_{L^{2}(\rho)}}{\delta_{n}^{b}}\longrightarrow\infty.

For p=∞p=\infty, the source itself has a bounded BV density.

We prove Proposition 4 in Section 4. Thus 1/41/4 is the optimal W2W_{2} exponent over the class of BV sources with finite second moment and bounded targets.

=∫⟨x,Tμ​(x)⟩​dρ​(x)−∫⟨x,y⟩​dσ​(x,y)⩾0.\displaystyle=\int\langle x,T_{\mu}(x)\rangle\,\mathrm{d}\rho(x)-\int\langle x,y\rangle\,\mathrm{d}\sigma(x,y)\geqslant 0.

When supp⁡μ⊂B¯​(0,R)\operatorname{supp}\mu\subset\overline{B}(0,R), we choose ϕ\phi globally convex and RR-Lipschitz by taking the supremum of its supporting affine functions with slopes in this ball. Define its Moreau–Yosida regularization and the corresponding gap by

ϕt​(x)=infz{ϕ⁡(z)+|x−z|22​t},𝒢t​(σ)=∫gϕt​𝑑σ,t>0.\phi_{t}(x)=\inf_{z}{\biggl\{\phi(z)+\frac{|x-z|^{2}}{2t}\biggr\}},\qquad\mathcal{G}_{t}(\sigma)=\int g_{\phi_{t}}\,\mathrm{d}\sigma,\quad t>0. (10)

ϕt∗​(y)=ϕ∗​(y)+t2​|y|2.\phi_{t}^{*}(y)=\phi^{*}(y)+\frac{t}{2}|y|^{2}. (11)

For the properties of the envelope, see Moreau [17] and Bauschke–Combettes [1, Chapter 12]. The proof has three steps: estimate the regularization error, use coercivity of the regularized gap, and bound the original gap by the target distance through a suitable coupling.

Lemma 6 (Stability of the duality gap).

Assume (1), and set Hp=Λ​B01/p′H_{p}=\Lambda B_{0}^{1/p^{\prime}}. For any convex RR-Lipschitz function ϕ\phi, define almost everywhere

at=ϕt−ϕ+t2​|∇ϕ|2,At=∫at​𝑑ρ.a_{t}=\phi_{t}-\phi+\frac{t}{2}|\nabla\phi|^{2},\qquad A_{t}=\int a_{t}\,\mathrm{d}\rho. (12)

Then

At⩽Hp2 31/p′​R2+1/p′​t1+1/p′.A_{t}\leqslant\frac{H_{p}}{2\,3^{1/p^{\prime}}}R^{2+1/p^{\prime}}t^{1+1/p^{\prime}}. (13)

If ∇ϕ\nabla\phi pushes ρ\rho to μ\mu, then for every σ∈Π⁡(ρ,μ)\sigma\in\Pi(\rho,\mu),

0⩽𝒢t​(σ)−𝒢⁡(σ)=𝒢t​(σ∗)=At.0\leqslant\mathcal{G}_{t}(\sigma)-\mathcal{G}(\sigma)=\mathcal{G}_{t}(\sigma_{*})=A_{t}. (14)
